lots.title: 2FE Mainstream Primary School - Schedule of Accommodation (420 places, 1 and 2 storey, single block)
lots.description: Accommodation programme for the 2-form entry mainstream primary element of the Stockport Town Centre School project. Recommended GIA is 2,081.9 m2 (excluding 15% uplift); SMBC has instructed the GIA be uplifted to 15% above BB103 recommended GIA, giving an approximate design target of 2,394 m2 (2,400 m2 rounded). The schedule is organised by functional zone: Basic Teaching Area (15 spaces / 881 m2 comprising reception, infant extensive, junior standard, and primary practical/food/science/DT), Large Spaces including halls and studios (2 spaces / 235 m2 with assembly hall suitable for 40 or 60 minute dining in 2-3 sittings, plus an activity studio reducible to 45 m2 music/drama studio under NOR 600), Learning Resource Areas (6 spaces / 85 m2 including a school library, medical treatment / MI room, SEN resource space, and small group rooms), Staff and Administration (9 spaces / 130 m2 including staff room and workroom which may be combined into a minimum 47 m2 space, head office, offices with meeting area, reprographics, reception and entrance, confidential interview rooms, first aid / sick bay), Storage (40 spaces / 146 m2 split between teaching storage, non-teaching storage, cloakrooms/coat stores, cleaners and maintenance stores), and Non-net Area covering kitchen suite, kitchen dry store, kitchen staff toilets/changing, supervisable early years toilets, pupil toilet suites, hygiene rooms with hoist and changing bed, staff toilets, accessible toilets, plant and service shafts, and server rooms. SMBC design assumptions include: restricted town-centre site, 1 and 2 storey new construction in a single block, infant practicals in classrooms, junior practicals in specialist spaces, single library accessed by infants and juniors, servery used as dining furniture storage, hall storage at 10% of hall size, and secure storage is required. Uplift beneficiaries identified by SMBC include secure reception area, corridor width, number of small group rooms, and a parents/club room (20-50 m2) with kitchenette facilities adjoining a hall for wrap-around care, holiday clubs and case conferences.
requirements: Total Gross Internal Area (GIA) 2,081.9 m2 per BB103 recommendation, uplifted by 15% on SMBC instruction to approximately 2,394 m2

Basic Teaching Area totalling 881 m2 across 15 spaces: 2 reception classrooms at 62 m2 each with sink/drainer, 4 infant extensive classrooms at 62 m2 for practical activities in-classroom, 8 junior standard classrooms at 55 m2, 1 primary practical room for food/science/DT at 69 m2 with bench/sink/cooker arrangements (one workstation per 3-5 pupils)
Large spaces: 1 assembly hall (150 m2) suitable for 40 or 60 minute dining in 2 or 3 sittings, plus 1 activity studio (85 m2) usable as a music/drama studio and reducible to 45 m2 under NOR 600
Learning Resource Areas: 1 school library (34 m2), 1 medical treatment/MI room (12 m2), 1 SEN resource space (12 m2) suitable for SEND and multi-agency use, 3 small group rooms (9 m2 each)

Staff and Administration: 1 staff room (41 m2) combinable with 1 staff workroom (13 m2) into a single space of minimum 47 m2, 1 head's office (16 m2), 1 office with meeting area (9 m2), 1 enclosed office with reception desk (20 m2), 1 reprographics room (11 m2), 1 reception/entrance (10 m2 with 50% circulation), 1 confidential interview room (6 m2), 1 first aid / sick bay (4 m2, increased to minimum 6 m2 if a dedicated sick room)

Storage: 40 spaces / 146 m2 including classroom stores off reception (2 x 3 m2), classroom stores off infants and juniors (12 x 1.5 m2), specialist teaching resource store (5 m2) with laptop trolley recharge capacity, internal sports equipment store at 10% of hall size, external sports equipment store, dining furniture stores/servery, secure storeroom, coat/bag stores, early-years cloakroom, cleaners' stores, maintenance equipment stores

Non-net Area / Kitchen and sanitary: 1 full-service kitchen prep/servery suite (58 m2, includes capacity for primary Resource Base pupils), kitchen dry store (3 m2), kitchen staff toilet with changing area (4 m2), 6 supervisable early-years toilets (2 WCs per reception class), 3 pupil toilet suites (18 WCs across remaining pupils, equal boys/girls), 1 hygiene room with hoist, changing bed, accessible WC, and either a sluice or waste-management facility plus storage for pads/spare clothing, 1 staff toilet suite (2 WCs), 2 accessible/staff toilets (one per floor), plant and service shafts (49 m2), servers (10.2 m2)

SMBC design brief: restricted town-centre site, 1 and 2 storey new construction, single block, all general classrooms standard size, single library accessed by infant and junior pupils, servery doubles as dining furniture storage, hall storage at 10% of hall size, secure storage required

lots.title: 2-Class Primary Resource Base - Schedule of Accommodation (16 SEND pupils)
lots.description: Accommodation programme for the 2-class primary Resource Base element, delivering an additional 193 m2 GIA adjoining the 2FE primary school. Provides two resource-base classrooms at 52 m2 each (with sink and drainer, zoned for any key stage including EYFS and sized for 8 pupils per class) and associated support spaces: 1 small group room (9 m2), 1 staff workroom (12 m2), 1 resource base store (5 m2), and 1 hygiene room (8 m2) with hoist, changing bed, accessible WC and waste/sluice provision. Assumes Resource Base pupils access the primary school assembly halls for PE and dining, access the primary practical room via easy-access pathway, and access the main school staff WCs (no separate staff toilet suite provided). Where quiet dining is required, seating can be accommodated in Food Tech, Parents Room or Classrooms per the Primary SoA. The Resource Base should have easy access to the main school hygiene room; if not, a hygiene room is re-provided within the Resource Base as listed.

warnings.message: This document is a Schedule of Accommodation (a technical-specification annex / design brief for the Stockport Town Centre School). It is NOT a procurement-lot-defining tender pack. The four 'lots' emitted (SoA-1 .. SoA-4) correspond to the four distinct accommodation programmes the document presents (2FE Primary mainstream, 2-class Primary Resource Base, 5FE Secondary mainstream, 4-class Secondary Resource Base). They are space-programme deliverables for the overall design-team appointment, not independently biddable procurement lots.
evidence_refs: document_title=Schedule of Accommodation & Calculations DRAFT (To be read)

warnings.message: The Schedule of Accommodation does not contain bidder evaluation criteria or weighting text. Evaluation criteria arrays are intentionally left empty for all four lots. Evaluation criteria for this procurement live in the separate Invitation-to-Participate / Instructions and Response Document annexes, not in this schedule.

The Schedule of Accommodation does not cite any CPV codes. CPV assignment for this tender is published at the process/notice level (category '150000 - Consultancy' per notice metadata) and is not duplicated in this schedule. cpv_codes arrays are intentionally left empty for all four lots.

The source document does not number its accommodation programmes as procurement lots. Lot identifiers SoA-1..SoA-4 are synthetic labels derived from the four Docling sections (#/groups/0..3). The five existing notice_lots rows at the process level (Architect Annex A.1, CDM PD Annex A.4, Structural Annex A.5, etc.) are per-discipline scope lots and are orthogonal to these four accommodation programmes; the daemon should not attempt to merge or replace them based on this extraction.

Because this tender is a design-team appointment (multi-disciplinary consultancy), the product_requirement_seeds emitted describe building fit-out elements and specialist rooms (kitchen suite, hygiene room hoist, sports hall, science laboratories, DT workshops, drama/music suite, dining area, Resource Base classroom fit-out). They are upstream design requirements, not goods that the buyer will purchase under this procurement. Downstream consumers should expect these seeds to feed construction-stage product discovery (future contracts), not the current Consultancy appointment.

Source PDF extraction was generated from an .xlsx workbook; Docling collapsed all six sheets into page_start=1, page_end=1 for every section. Evidence anchors therefore rely on the Docling section_ref (#/groups/0..5) and the sheet heading as the primary locator, not on meaningful PDF page numbers.
